newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 19.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 19.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

** The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 11.47 points at 5,877.36 on Wednesday as news of a widening U.S. trade deficit in July raised doubts about the economy's strength and whether the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates.

** Australia's powerful Maritime Union on Wednesday launched rolling bans on Indonesian shipping to protest against the arrest of Indonesian labour leaders and Canberra's "failure" to press Jakarta on human rights.

** An International Monetary Fund report said on Wednesday Indonesia had made significant improvements in its banking system recently but some banks remained vulnerable to macroeconomic imbalances and disturbances.
** The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.25 points, or 0.40 percent, to close at 559.70 points on Wednesday due to falls in few big-capitalised stocks.
** Brokers said players were expected to open weak on Thursday following overnight falls on Wall Street.
** On Thursday, the Indonesian rupiah was at 2,317.30/17.75 in early trading against an opening of 2,318.50/19.50.
** Photographic equipment distributor Inter Delta on market talk of a possible acquisition.
** Astra on fresh market talk of a possible takeover and rights issue. The firm has declined to comment on the take-over talk but said there was no plan to announce a rights issue.
** Pudjiadi & Sons on announcement that the hotel and property firm planned to buy a stake in a hotel management consulting firm.

** Summarecon on market talk that the property firm had secured a deal to build a toll road in West Java. The firm has denied the talk but said its new apartment project in north Jakarta was a success.
